research_question: Among adolescents aged approximately 12–18 years, what is the short-term effect of combined dietary and physical activity interventions delivered through school-, community-, or family-based programmes, compared with no intervention, usual curriculum, or usual care, on BMI in kg/m² at the first post-intervention assessment occurring no more than 12 months after the intervention ends?
treatment_label: Combined dietary and physical activity intervention (school-based, community-based, or family-based programme containing both components)
control_label: Concurrent control condition (no intervention, usual curriculum, or usual care)
outcome_description: Body mass index measured in kg/m² at the first assessment after the intervention ended, provided that assessment occurred no more than 12 months after intervention completion. Pool only BMI in kg/m²; do not combine BMI z-scores, BMI percentiles, waist circumference, body fat, dietary intake, physical activity, or other outcomes. Extract a directly reported adjusted or unadjusted between-group difference preferentially. Otherwise derive the intervention-minus-control difference from arm-level follow-up means or, if unavailable, mean changes from baseline. For multiple eligible short-term assessments, select the first post-intervention assessment. For multi-arm studies, combine all eligible intervention arms containing both diet and physical activity components where possible, or select the main eligible intervention arm, while using the control group only once.
positive_direction: For any standardized, direction-harmonized effect, a positive value would mean lower BMI and therefore a result favouring the combined intervention. For the user-requested raw mean difference, however, retain the specified intervention-minus-control orientation: MD below 0 kg/m² favours the intervention and MD above 0 kg/m² favours control.
search_queries: adolescent combined diet physical activity intervention controlled BMI trial
school family community nutrition exercise programme adolescent BMI comparison
teen obesity prevention diet physical activity controlled study BMI outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original quantitative studies of combined interventions containing both a dietary component and a physical activity component, delivered in school, community, family, or related settings to samples whose age range overlaps 12–18 years and in which most participants are adolescents.
Randomised or non-randomised controlled studies with a concurrent no-intervention, usual-curriculum, or usual-care comparison condition.

Studies reporting BMI in kg/m² at the first assessment after intervention completion and no later than 12 months afterward, with sufficient direct or derivable quantitative information for an intervention-versus-control mean difference and its standard error or variance.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between an eligible treatment group and a concurrent control condition, including uncontrolled pre–post studies.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size and uncertainty estimate, such as a between-group estimate with SE, confidence interval or p-value, or arm-level means with SDs and sample sizes; studies reporting only adjusted or model-predicted arm means are excluded if no SE for their difference can be derived.

Completely unrelated to the research topic or ineligible in a defining way, including diet-only or physical-activity-only programmes, samples not predominantly adolescent, BMI reported only as z-scores or percentiles, other adiposity or behavioural outcomes without BMI in kg/m², or assessments only beyond 12 months after intervention completion.
moderators_to_extract: study design (individual RCT, cluster RCT, or non-randomised controlled study)
delivery setting (school, community, family/home, or multisetting)
participant age range and mean age
intervention duration and time from intervention end to BMI assessment
intervention intensity and degree of parental/family involvement
risk-of-bias features and whether the extracted estimate was adjusted or unadjusted
effect_size_note: Use a random-effects model to pool mean differences (MDs) in BMI, expressed in kg/m² and oriented strictly as intervention minus control; therefore MD < 0 favours the intervention. Prefer a directly reported between-group difference, adjusted or unadjusted, with its SE. Derive SE from a two-sided 95% CI as (upper limit − lower limit)/3.92; where only a p-value and sample size are reported, derive the test statistic from the p-value using the reported analysis and degrees of freedom when available, then calculate SE = |estimate/test statistic|, documenting the assumptions and calculation. If no direct contrast is available, calculate the MD from end-of-follow-up arm means, SDs, and sample sizes; alternatively use arm-level mean changes and change-score SDs. Do not mix incompatible BMI units or substitute z-scores/percentiles. If BMI-specific analysed sample sizes are absent, use randomised or enrolled numbers per arm and flag this substitution; never leave group sizes blank. If only adjusted/model-predicted arm means are reported, subtract control from intervention, but exclude the comparison if its SE cannot be derived. For eligible multi-arm studies, combine eligible diet-plus-activity arms using standard Cochrane formulas for means, SDs, and sample sizes, or use the prespecified/main intervention arm, ensuring the shared control is counted once. Account for clustering using reported cluster-adjusted estimates where possible; otherwise apply a design-effect correction using an available or defensibly imputed ICC and report sensitivity analyses. Estimate between-study variance with a standard random-effects approach, report pooled MD with 95% CI, tau², and I², and assess robustness with influence/leave-one-out and risk-of-bias sensitivity analyses when enough studies are available.
